taxpayer.notes: W-2 employee of Marcus L. Ward Home, Inc. and Am Law Corp. in 2018; operated unincorporated business Total Life Transformation (TLT); advanced frivolous tax-protester arguments. Filing status not stated.

adjustments: unreported 2018 wages ($9,993/$9,994 from Ward) and $354 state tax refund
disallowed Schedule C commissions and fees ($6,000 2018; $5,500 2019)
disallowed Schedule C car and truck expenses ($26,978 2018; $32,190 2019)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: All adjustments, via frivolous/groundless arguments; no evidence presented

findings_of_fact.fact: Ward issued Form W-2 reporting 2018 wages of $9,994
findings_of_fact.snippet: Ward issued Mr. Morino Form W–2, Wage and Tax Statement, reporting that it paid him wages of $9,994 during 2018.

findings_of_fact.fact: New Jersey issued Form 1099-G reporting a $354 state income tax refund paid in 2018
findings_of_fact.snippet: reporting that the state paid him during 2018 a $354 refund of state income tax.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2018 return reported Am Law wages $7,917, unemployment $17,706, TLT business loss $19,129, student loan interest deduction $2,500
findings_of_fact.snippet: On that return Mr. Morino reported wages paid by Am Law totaling $7,917; unemployment compensation of $17,706; a business loss of $19,129 from TLT

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner did not dispute the transcript or receipt of the income, nor show no tax benefit from the prior deduction of state tax
findings_of_fact.snippet: Mr. Morino did not dispute the accuracy of the transcript or his receipt of this income.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2018 second Schedule C: gross income $41,499, expenses $60,628 incl. car/truck $26,978, commissions $6,000, other $15,050
findings_of_fact.snippet: The deducted expenses consisted of, inter alia, $26,978 in car and truck expenses, $6,000 in commissions and fees, and $15,050 in other expenses.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2019 second Schedule C: gross income $48,543, expenses $67,840 incl. car/truck $32,190, commissions $5,500, other $11,100; business loss $19,297
findings_of_fact.snippet: The deducted expenses consisted of, inter alia, $32,190 in car and truck expenses, $5,500 in commissions and fees, and $11,100 in other expenses.

findings_of_fact.fact: No testimony or evidence substantiating the deductions
findings_of_fact.snippet: At trial Mr. Morino failed to provide any testimony or other evidence to substantiate the claimed deductions.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2018 extension to Oct. 15, 2019; return filed April 17, 2020; no reasonable cause argued
findings_of_fact.snippet: Mr. Morino requested an extension of time to file his 2018 Form 1040, until October 15, 2019, as permitted by section 6081(a).
However, Mr. Morino filed his 2018 Form 1040 on April 17, 2020.

findings_of_fact.fact: Supervisor approved 6662 penalties per sec. 6751(b)(1); no reasonable-cause defense offered
findings_of_fact.snippet: Mr. Morino did not offer a reasonable cause defense to the imposition of the accuracy-related penalties.

findings_of_fact.fact: Warned by order of Jan. 24, 2024 and at trial about sec. 6673; first proceeding before the Court
findings_of_fact.snippet: Since this is Mr. Morino’s first time proceeding before this Court, we will not impose a penalty now.

issues.question: Did petitioner receive and fail to report 2018 wages of $9,993 and a $354 state tax refund includible in gross income?
issues.holding: Yes; third-party reported wages and state refund (tax benefit rule) included in 2018 gross income

amount_determined.description: unreported wages $9,994 (issue statement says $9,993) and state refund $354

issues.computable_reason: Undisputed receipt of third-party-reported amounts; inclusion under sec. 61 and tax benefit rule is mechanical

issues.question: (Schedule C deductions, sec. 162/274(d)) Is petitioner entitled to deduct commissions and fees, car and truck, and other expenses for 2018 and 2019?
issues.holding: No; no evidence substantiating any of the claimed expenses

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the sec. 6651(a)(1) addition to tax for 2018?
issues.holding: Liable; 2018 return filed April 17, 2020, after extended due date Oct. 15, 2019, and no reasonable cause argued or shown
issues.computable_reason: Lateness follows from filing date vs. extended due date; no reasonable-cause defense was raised

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for sec. 6662(a) negligence penalties for 2018 and 2019?
issues.holding: Liable; negligence/disregard shown, written supervisory approval, no reasonable cause defense
issues.computable_reason: Negligence ground and 6751(b) compliance are record/judgment findings, not threshold arithmetic

issues.question: (Sec. 6673 frivolous-position penalty) Should the Court impose a sec. 6673(a)(1) penalty?
issues.holding: No penalty imposed because it is petitioner's first proceeding; warned for future

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent.
decision.summary: Deficiencies, 2018 6651(a)(1) addition and 6662(a) penalties sustained; no 6673 penalty

notes: No stipulation; six unobjected exhibits plus testimony. Opinion rounds to dollars; issue statement says wages $9,993 but facts say W-2 $9,994. First 2018 Schedule C: gross $22,249 offset by equal 'management fee'; first 2019 Schedule C: gross $26,163 offset likewise. Other-expense itemizations on pp. 3-4 sum to $15,050 (2018) and $11,100 (2019), while disputed 'other expenses' are $8,920 and $5,820 (derived: IRS apparently allowed part). Remaining adjustments computational.
